as_told.title: Dr Powell's medical license revoked for researching telepathy

plain: A doctor named Diane Powell lost her medical licence, the story goes, because she looked into telepathy, the idea that one mind can pick up another's thoughts without words. Michels raises it while talking with the filmmaker Ky Dickens, who made The Telepathy Tapes, a documentary about children said to read minds. He calls it an "atrocity" that Powell's licence "was revoked at one point right just for looking into this stuff." In a later episode he says it more sharply: "Her medical license got revoked for studying these telepathic children," and he credits The Telepathy Tapes. Dickens, passing on what Powell told her, ties it to something else. She says it happened when Powell wrote her book The ESP Enigma, about ESP, short for extrasensory perception, meaning knowledge that comes from somewhere other than the ordinary senses: "she had her medical license revoked because she was talking about ESP." So the two tellers disagree on the cause, a book or the work with the children. Either way, if it is true, a doctor was punished by her own profession for studying the subject.
